summary: Belgium publishes police counts of sexual offences against minors but no nationality or origin of child victims or offenders for any harm; parliamentary requests for suspects' nationality were answered 'not available' or not at all. The only origin data are supported trafficking victims by nationality.

nations.National (Federal Police, Myria): Police figures released in parliamentary answers; Myria trafficking report.

european_title: Not recorded by any Belgian source
european_note: Belgian official statistics record no ethnic origin, and nationality is published only for supported trafficking victims. 'Belgian' includes naturalised citizens and 'foreign' mixes Europeans and non-Europeans, so ethnic Europeans cannot be identified.
proxy_note: Belgium records citizenship for supported trafficking victims only, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Sexual offences against minors (police)
harms.intro: Federal Police data released in answer to Chamber written question 719 (30 Oct 2025) give offences with minor victims: 2,011 rapes and 2,674 other offences against sexual integrity in 2024, plus 284 voyeurism offences. The sexual criminal code was reformed in June 2022, which affects trends. No nationality of victims or suspects is given. A news site (Doorbraak.be, non-government) cites a foreign share of suspects of sexual offences, but with no primary source; it is not used.

victims.text: Federal Police statistics on offences against minors are released without nationality; asked for it, the Minister answered that the information is not available.

perpetrators.text: No nationality or origin of suspects or convicted people is published. Senate written questions 8-344 and 8-399 asking for the nationality of suspects of sexual offences against children had no published answer when checked.

cross.text: Neither side is published by any origin variable.

harms.label: Physical abuse (Flemish child-abuse centres)
harms.intro: No national statistics on physical child abuse by origin. The six Vertrouwenscentra Kindermishandeling (recognised and subsidised by the Flemish government) received 7,501 reports involving 10,913 children in 2024; 3,200 children were in reports of physical abuse or neglect. No origin variable is published.

victims.text: The Flemish child-abuse centres publish reports and children by type of abuse with no origin variable.

perpetrators.text: No nationality or origin of suspects or convicted people is published. Senate written questions 8-344 and 8-399 asking for the nationality of suspects of sexual offences against children had no published answer when checked.

harms.label: Trafficking victims supported by the specialised centres
harms.intro: The three specialised centres (Payoke, PAG-ASA and Sürya) began supporting 142 trafficking victims in 2024: 77 for economic exploitation, 50 for sexual exploitation and 6 for forced criminality among the 135 single-form cases. Myria, the federal migration centre, publishes them by exploitation type, sex, age (under or over 18) and nationality. Only victims who enter support are counted.

victims.scope: Belgium, trafficking victims newly supported by the specialised centres, all ages and forms, 2024
victims.share_note: Moroccan (29), Belgian (23), Brazilian (14), Colombian (11) and Afghan (8) citizens were the largest groups. Of the 50 victims of sexual exploitation, 14 were Belgian, 11 Brazilian and 8 Colombian. Foreign = 142 minus 23 Belgian, calculated here. Citizenship, not ethnicity: Belgian statistics do not record ethnic origin.

perpetrators.text: Myria reports final convictions for trafficking (104 in 2023, from the Justice Ministry criminal-policy service) without the nationality of the people convicted.

cross.text: No table links victim and trafficker nationality.

data.scope: Belgium (mainly Wallonia and Brussels), presumed minor trafficking victims taken in by the Esperanto centre, 2015-2024

data.share_note: Serbian (25), Belgian (16, all girls in sexual exploitation) and Romanian (15) minors were most frequent. Myria's 2026 study of minor victims reports that the French-speaking youth-aid administration (AGAJ) often ticks Belgian nationality by default when recording minors. Citizenship, not ethnicity: Belgian statistics do not record ethnic origin.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm. Heritage points require that link as a published cross-table for the same child cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points and is awarded only for a published cross-table that records child victim heritage and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage. Coverage is 10, rates 7.5 and access 7.5. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points, and only when that pair is published. A published “White” category that merges Hispanic people or another group, so ethnic Europeans cannot be isolated, is scored as a proxy under the same cap. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%. Neglect is not part of the score.
score.why: Belgium scores 6% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Heritage points are 0 because there is no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data earns no heritage credit. Federal Police statistics on sexual offences against minors are released without nationality (the Minister answered that it is not available), and no national source gives the origin of child victims or offenders for any harm. The only origin data are Myria's figures on supported trafficking victims by nationality.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 24 Nov 2026 (homicide 27.78, sexual abuse 22.22, sex trafficking 22.22, physical abuse 16.67, online exploitation 11.11); paired-data rule: heritage points only for a published child victim×offender cross-table

paired_child.basis: No published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.

sv719.name: Answer to Chamber written question 719 (Van Hoecke) on sexual offences against minors

sv719.records: Offences against sexual integrity, rape, voyeurism and grooming with minor victims.
sv719.limitations: No nationality ("information not available"). The answer was read from a copy hosted by the party of the MP who asked it (Vlaams Belang); the figures are the official answer.
